_about: Deployment targets for `python afm.py deploy --target NAME` (STANDARD.md section 8).
Placeholders {name} are filled from --set name=value, then the environment variable AFM_DEPLOY_<NAME>, then the target's defaults, then the common defaults below.
`builtin` targets run Python code in pipeline/deploy.py. Other targets run `commands` in order, or, when `check` is given: `check` decides between `update` (it succeeds) and `create` (it fails).
`external: true` means the target changes something outside this computer: the commands are shown and confirmed before they run.
Never put secret values here or in --set. Cloud targets read secrets from the provider's secret store by name or ARN.
The cloud commands follow each provider's documentation as of October 2026; check them against the current documentation before the first real run.

local.description: This computer, without Docker: build the pages, then run the server

docker.description: This computer, in the container (docker compose), data kept in a volume
docker.after: Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 (or the AFM_HOST_PORT in .env). Stop: docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down

static.description: The built pages and a start page as plain files, for any static file host (no API)

image.description: Build the container image and push it to a registry
image.needs: Docker, signed in to the registry (docker login)

cloudrun.description: Google Cloud Run: deploy the image as a Cloud Run service (creates or updates)
cloudrun.needs: gcloud, signed in; the image pushed to Artifact Registry (target image); three secrets in Secret Manager
cloudrun.notes: Create the secrets afm-jwt-secret, afm-vault-master-key and afm-admin-password in Secret Manager first, and let the service account read them. Cloud Run has no persistent disk: backend data is lost on restart (STANDARD.md 8.4).

ecs.description: Amazon ECS Express Mode: create the service (Fargate, load balancer, scaling) from the image
ecs.needs: aws CLI v2, signed in; the image pushed to ECR (target image); the task execution role and the Express infrastructure role; three secrets in Secrets Manager
ecs.notes: The execution role must be allowed to read the three secrets. To roll out a new image to an existing service: aws ecs update-express-gateway-service --service-arn <arn> --primary-container '{...}'. No persistent disk: backend data is lost on restart (STANDARD.md 8.4).

azure.description: Azure Container Apps: create the container app, or update its image if it exists
azure.needs: az CLI with the containerapp extension, signed in; a Container Apps environment; the image in Azure Container Registry; a user-assigned identity that can pull from the registry and read the Key Vault secrets
create: az containerapp create --name {service} --resource-group {resource_group} --environment {environment} --image {image} --target-port 8080 --ingress external --registry-server {registry_server} --registry-identity {identity} --user-assigned {identity} --secrets jwt-secret=keyvaultref:{key_vault_url}/secrets/afm-jwt-secret,identityref:{identity} vault-key=keyvaultref:{key_vault_url}/secrets/afm-vault-master-key,identityref:{identity} admin-password=keyvaultref:{key_vault_url}/secrets/afm-admin-password,identityref:{identity} --env-vars AFM_ENV=production AFM_ENABLE_API={api} AFM_JWT_SECRET=secretref:jwt-secret AFM_VAULT_MASTER_KEY=secretref:vault-key AFM_PLATFORM_ADMIN_PASSWORD=secretref:admin-password
azure.notes: registry is the ACR login server, e.g. aifirstmart.azurecr.io; identity is the user-assigned identity's resource id; key_vault_url is e.g. https://<vault>.vault.azure.net. Container Apps has no persistent disk by default: backend data is lost on restart (STANDARD.md 8.4).

server.description: Your own Linux server: copy deploy/ and .env, pull the image, restart it
server.needs: SSH access (key-based) to the server; Docker with the compose plugin on the server, signed in to the registry
commands: ssh {host} "cd {dir} && chmod 600 .env && AFM_IMAGE={image} docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml pull && AFM_IMAGE={image} docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d --no-build"
server.notes: host is user@address. Publish the image first (target image, or a release pushes it to ghcr.io/ilangoj). Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS (Caddy, nginx) in front of port 8080.
